newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil loses ground amid good supplies.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil loses ground amid good supplies.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil failed to ignite on Friday despite the big freeze gripping much of Europe.
Traders said high sulphur barges lost $1 or so amid bunker demand of around 15,000 tonnes. Traders said activity petered out by mid-afternoon.
The high sulphur cargo market gained little support from the weather and increased electricity demand.
"Utilities seem happy to sit it out, they have stocks to cover this eventuality, but they may have to come into the market if the cold persists for much longer," said one trader at a major.
Prices were pegged around $109 fob NWE, but could climb next week. "There isn't a great deal of material around, prices could be squeezed higher," said a dealer.
One dealer thought Portugal might tender next week.
Low sulphur fuel supplies look good which has knocked $1-2 off prices. At least 150,000 tonnes was available for early Jan with more pieces in the sidelines.
"It will need a hefty amount of demand to clear," said a trader. Wet prices were close to paper levels of $123-124 fob for Jan.
